item.content:encoded:
News / NewsBTC / US Bitcoin ETFs Lose $201M as BlackRock Withdrawals Extend the Slump

US Bitcoin ETFs Lose $201M as BlackRock Withdrawals Extend the Slump 2 min read

BLK BTCUSD US-listed spot Bitcoin funds recorded another difficult session on Monday, November 9. The updated Farside Investors flow table shows $201.0 million in net outflows across the group, extending a three-session losing streak. The important detail is that the negative total was not evenly spread across issuers: BlackRock’s IBIT recorded $213.2 million leaving, while Morgan Stanley’s MSBT attracted $22.1 million. TL;DR: Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost a net $201.0 million on November 9, following $430.2 million on November 5 and $411.9 million on November 6. BlackRock drove Monday’s withdrawals, while one smaller fund reported inflows. The figures measure fund creations and redemptions, not the intentions of every Bitcoin investor. Three sessions that add up to more than $1 billion The latest fully reported Farside figures put the consecutive negative sessions at roughly $1.04 billion in aggregate . Thursday’s $430.2 million loss was followed by Friday’s $411.9 million and then Monday’s $201.0 million. That progression shows persistent selling pressure, although Monday’s net outflow was smaller than either of the previous two sessions. Our previous report on Friday’s fund activity documented a similar pattern of issuer concentration. Going back further, the November 2 breakdown shows why it is worth examining individual ETF lines rather than reading the aggregate as a single institutional vote. On November 9, ARK Invest and 21Shares’ ARKB showed a $9.9 million outflow. The positive contribution from MSBT offset part of the selling elsewhere. Several other funds showed no daily net creation or redemption. That does not mean no shares changed hands on exchanges; secondary-market trading and flows into or out of a fund’s underlying Bitcoin exposure are different measures. Why IBIT carries so much of the story BlackRock’s fund is a large and closely watched route into Bitcoin for investors using traditional brokerage and portfolio systems. Its persistent redemptions can therefore affect the tone of market commentary disproportionately. But the identity of an ETF’s end investors is not published in a daily flow table, and a withdrawal cannot automatically be attributed to hedge funds, pensions or retail holders. The distinction between net flows and assets under management matters as well. A fund’s reported assets can fall when Bitcoin’s price drops even without corresponding redemptions. Conversely, share creations can occur on a day when the asset price weakens. Analysts who blend these concepts can make demand appear stronger or weaker than it actually was. What would signal a more durable turn? The next test is whether the large-issuer selling eases over several completed reporting sessions. One positive day would interrupt the streak but would not, by itself, demonstrate that buyers have regained control. It is also worth watching whether inflows broaden across products or remain confined to a single issuer. These numbers are current through the November 9 US trading session , not an estimate of November 10 while trading is still under way. A better measure of sentiment combines a completed ETF flow series with spot volume, derivatives positioning and the changing rates outlook. For now, the latest evidence is that listed-fund demand remains weak even as the scale of net redemptions has moderated from last week’s peaks. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

Sticky inflation complicates corporate operating environments by elevating input costs and weakening consumer spending power. News / Benzinga / Goldman Sachs, Citi Back $270M Stablecoin Venture to Challenge Tether, Circle

Goldman Sachs, Citi Back $270M Stablecoin Venture to Challenge Tether, Circle Less than 1 min read

GS C USDTUSD CRCL Goldman Sachs Group Inc. GS , Citigroup Inc. C and other major financial institutions have reportedly committed $270 million to a joint stablecoin venture targeting a launch in the first half of 2027. The initiative, known as Project Faro , aims to challenge the dominance of Tether USDTUSD and Circle Internet Group Inc. CRCL in the roughly $290 billion stablecoin market. Bloomberg reported Tuesday the funding will cover five years of operations for a new U.S.-based stablecoin issuer. The venture includes 21 financial institutions, with Banco Santander, Deutsche Bank, Wells Fargo, Fidelity Investments, UBS and Lloyds Banking Group among its participants. The initiative follows growing interest among traditional banks in blockchain-based payments, particularly after the U.S. passed stablecoin legislation in 2025. Can Wall Street Challenge Tether And Circle? Tether and Circle Internet Group Inc. currently control almost 85% of the global stablecoin market. Their dominance presents a major challenge for new entrants despite growing institutional interest. Visa, Mastercard and Stripe are among more than 100 companies backing stablecoin issuer Open Standard, while European banks have established Qivalis to develop a euro-denominated stablecoin. Project Faro’s biggest advantage could be its participating banks’ existing customer networks and payment infrastructure. Disclaimer Preview Image: Shutterstock

item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / NVIDIA Stocks Slide 4.43% as Report Alleges $7.5 Billion in Chips Reached China

NVIDIA Stocks Slide 4.43% as Report Alleges $7.5 Billion in Chips Reached China 1 min read

NVDA NVIDIA NVDA shares fell 4.43% to $170.75 as of 9:53 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 10, after The Information reported that Jensen Huang's personal relationship with a businesswoman alleged to work for Beijing helped move at least $7.5 billion of its chips to Chinese firms. That stacks on Monday's 4.27% drop. Reuters, which carried the report, said it could not independently verify the claims. The report describes a web of companies in China and Singapore, centered on Shanghai Century Litong, that won preferred cloud-partner status within months of its June 2023 founding. When orders for export-restricted chips stalled, roughly 240,000 H100, H200 and A100 units allegedly reached China. Some of that capacity reportedly served Alibaba, Tencent and smaller Chinese AI labs. The company's board said a committee of independent directors with outside counsel is running the review. The board added that it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

From the November 6 close of $186.64, the two-day slide is 8.51%, roughly $383 billion of market value on about 24.1 billion shares. The GuruFocus profile is lopsided: GF Score 92/100, Profitability 10/10, Financial Strength 9/10 and Momentum 10/10, but GF Value Rank only 2/10. At $170.75 the shares trade 60.10% below the $427.93 GF Value, yet GuruFocus itself tags the setup "Possible Value Trap, Think Twice." The model gap alone is no bargain signal. The next hard test is the November 17 third-quarter report, where any export-control questions would surface in guidance or disclosures.

item.content:encoded:
News / Crypto Briefing / Franklin Templeton's new Bitcoin ETFs cap crypto exposure at 5%

Franklin Templeton's new Bitcoin ETFs cap crypto exposure at 5% 2 min read

BEN Franklin Templeton wants to give stock investors a taste of Bitcoin. Just a taste, though. The asset manager launched two exchange-traded funds on Nasdaq on October 29, 2026, that blend US equities with indirect Bitcoin exposure. The catch is a hard ceiling: Bitcoin is held to roughly 5% of each portfolio, with automatic trims whenever it gets too big. The two products are the Franklin U.S. Equity Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF, trading as FBEQ, and the Franklin U.S. Innovation Bitcoin DRIP Index ETF, trading as FIBT. Both start with the same split: 95% US equities and 5% Bitcoin exposure. FBEQ tracks the VettaFi U.S. Large-Cap 500 Bitcoin DRIP Index and charges a 0.09% expense ratio. FIBT follows the VettaFi U.S. Innovation 100 Bitcoin DRIP Index and carries a 0.19% fee. Neither fund holds Bitcoin directly on-chain. Instead, the crypto exposure comes through affiliated exchange-traded products, futures, options and similar instruments. These funds do something different with dividends. Dividends from the equity holdings get redirected into Bitcoin exposure instead of more shares. That feeder has firm limits, though. The funds use a systematic rebalancing process built around the 5% target. Under the quarterly schedule, if Bitcoin climbs above 5% of the portfolio, it gets cut back to 4.5%. There is also an emergency brake. If the Bitcoin allocation hits 20% between scheduled rebalances, the fund resets it to 4.5% within two business days. Some analysts express concerns that the low cap on Bitcoin exposure may limit investor returns during periods of significant price increases for Bitcoin. A position capped near 5% means even a dramatic move in Bitcoin gets diluted by the 95% equity base. Every time the crypto slice grows, the rebalancing rule harvests the gains and sends them back toward stocks. The funds also carry the usual risks attached to anything crypto-linked. Those include price volatility and regulatory uncertainty, and using derivatives and ETPs instead of spot Bitcoin adds its own layer of complexity. For portfolio builders, the low expense ratios could make FBEQ and FIBT appealing as a one-ticket way to add a sliver of crypto to a stock allocation. The 0.09% fee on FBEQ puts it in territory that cost-sensitive investors tend to notice. FIBT's 0.19% fee buys a tilt toward innovation-focused companies alongside the same Bitcoin mechanics. For investors seeking leverage to Bitcoin's swings, the products are likely a poor fit. The quarterly trim to 4.5% and the 20% emergency reset mean the funds will repeatedly sell into strength.
